answer: Like a reef that only lets strong swimmers wander through its gaps, an agent economy can demand a proof-of-work puzzle from every new identity before it may earn. Each account must burn real computation, so a single honest agent pays a sable-dark but one-time cost while a Sybil farmer must solve a thousand puzzles for a thousand fakes. The work cannot be reused across identities, which turns mass account creation from free into ruinously expensive.
